idea.description: Provisional experiment: add a compact, jointly trained pooled-title/description residual to the corrected HSTU item embedding. Use the identical effective embedding for histories and candidate scoring, with exactly one trained checkpoint per category. Retain pooling as the initial controlled experiment; a whole-field character CNN is a subsequent alternative, not a simultaneous modification.
idea.motivation: At early research progress, a localized representation change offers a controlled test of interaction-supervised lexical sharing. It could address broad thematic matches and missed identifier or format distinctions, and reduce positive–negative ranking errors. These remain prospective hypotheses: user diagnosis contains no observations, and model diagnosis reports execution failure without measured behavior. No diagnosis-qualified best idea can currently be selected. Mean pooling distinguishes different retained token multisets, including identifiers and numbers, but cannot distinguish their order or establish compatibility, numerical relationships, negation scope, or current user need.
idea.implementation_notes:
Recovery and protocol: the corrected baseline source and underlying exception are absent, so this remains an integration specification rather than a reliable executable train.py patch. Obtain the actual training exception and restore executable baseline behavior before attributing failure to an architectural component. Do not infer the cause from CalledProcessError. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl and their routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per completed epoch, single-GPU execution, supplied splits, optimizer, objective, batch size, clipping, validation schedule, checkpoint selection, and stopping behavior. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory; charge training, diagnostics, controls, debugging, and failures to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No test inspection, external data, pretrained weights, other-trial checkpoints, or evaluator changes.

Initialization: construct and initialize the entire corrected baseline first, in its original order. Initialize new modules inside torch.random.fork_rng covering every touched device; isolate any added Python/NumPy randomness as well. Do not recursively initialize the wrapped identity embedding. Verify original baseline parameter equality and RNG restoration before training. The zero residual gate preserves initial effective embeddings; it does not guarantee the subsequent optimization trajectory remains identical.

Deterministic text specification: use only host-permitted public titles/descriptions and training interactions. Never use unavailable reviews, ratings, prices, stores, or item categories. Use catalog metadata only under the host's existing availability policy, without vocabulary decisions based on held-out interactions. Normalize text with Unicode NFKC and casefold. Tokenize with the fixed regex [a-z0-9]+(?:[._/+:-][a-z0-9]+)*|[^\s], retaining repeated tokens and punctuation. This is an explicit default rather than a validated optimum. Build a category-local vocabulary of at most 10,000 entries, reserving PAD=0 and UNK=1; select remaining tokens by descending corpus occurrence count with lexicographic ties. Retain the first 16 title tokens and 64 description tokens, pooling the fields separately. Treat a missing/empty field as zero, distinguish missing text from OOV text, and log coverage, OOV, and truncation rates. Apply these exact transformations in prediction through serialized item-token buffers and tokenizer assets.

Representation: use shared 32-dimensional scratch token embeddings initialized normally with standard deviation 0.02, masked field means, their concatenation, and a bias-free Xavier-initialized projection to the baseline item width. Padding token embeddings remain zero. Define e(i)=ID(i)+tanh(alpha)*stop_gradient(norm(ID(i)))*u(i), where u(i)=projected_text(i)/max(norm(projected_text(i)),1e-3), and alpha is one shared trainable scalar per category initialized to zero. Compute normalization and residual addition in FP32 with autocast disabled, then restore the baseline dtype. Clamp handling means u can have norm below one. Missing text and padding receive exactly zero residual; effective padding rows are exactly zero. Preserve any baseline embedding multiplier at its original location. Deduplicate requested item IDs for efficient differentiable text computation and gather back to their original shapes; never train through detached catalog caches. Register every added parameter in the baseline optimizer using its existing regularization policy.

Gate behavior: at alpha=0, encoder task gradients through this branch are zero, while the gate may receive a nonzero gradient from the random text directions. Encoder learning can begin on a subsequent pass if the gate moves; cancellation can prevent activation. Detaching the ID norm blocks gradients through that scale, not through the encoder. Log alpha, tanh(alpha), gate task gradient and actual update, encoder task-gradient norms and updates, pre-normalization text norms, and lexical-to-ID norm ratios on valid rows. For unit text directions and nonzero ID vectors, the ratio equals abs(tanh(alpha)); under norm clamping it is smaller. Separate None gradients from numerical zeros, measure after mixed-precision unscaling, and distinguish task-gradient updates from weight decay. Persistent inactivity should trigger inspection of optimizer registration, detachment, skipped updates, or per-example cancellation. Large absolute alpha also suppresses the gate derivative. Any nonzero-gate alternative is a separately recorded configuration, not an undocumented repair.

Compatibility and diagnosis: preserve item_emb(ids), baseline-required embedding attributes, effective weight access, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and host ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. All history and candidate representations use the same effective embedding. Compute full effective tables in chunks when required. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); return measured metrics and metric_definitions. Loader batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Measure ranking errors from actual model scores at valid supervised positions and embedding diagnostics from effective embeddings. Define each metric explicitly and mark unavailable observations unavailable; mean cosine near zero alone does not establish collapse or recommendation diversity. Read the greatest absolute nonpadding position, never count-1, retaining the supplied empty-history policy.

Checkpoint and predictor: serialize architecture configuration, lexical assets, vocabulary/tokenization settings, identity and lexical weights, gate, and backbone together. Update the embedded predictor writer with identical definitions. Each category loads exactly one selected independently trained checkpoint with strict state loading and model.eval(). Begin without an inference cache. If caching is required, build effective vectors in chunks under inference_mode only after loading and fixing device/dtype; invalidate on parameter, state, metadata, device, or dtype changes. Verify loaded-versus-original and cached-versus-uncached scores using documented tolerances and inspect any rank/tie changes. Include left-padded, repeated-item, all-padding, missing-text, and OOV cases. inference_mode alone does not disable dropout.

Experimental matrix and shortcuts: predeclare ID-only and aligned pooled-text configurations using existing host selection rules. Schedule a third matched-shuffle control only if remaining budget permits a complete four-category configuration. For that control, retrain the same text architecture with one fixed item-to-text permutation within train-interaction frequency bins 0-5, 6-20, and at least 21, additionally matching field-presence masks and retained field lengths exactly. Permute paired title/description records together, preserve missing-text masks, retain singleton strata unchanged, and report how many records actually moved. Generate permutations in sorted item order with a local NumPy RNG seed 42; serialize them and use them consistently during training and inference. Restricted shuffling may leave substantial alignment intact. Aligned text outperforming this control supports useful alignment beyond the matched measured properties, but does not prove semantic understanding or eliminate unmeasured confounding. Each configuration has one jointly trained network per category and no prediction fusion. Do not select categories across configurations. Log every attempted configuration, evaluation, failure, selected epoch, and GPU cost; do not treat incomplete configurations as complete comparisons.

Alternative CNN: if pooled text is executable and informative, consider a separately declared whole-field character CNN trained from scratch, preserving punctuation, digits, spaces, and field boundaries. Filters operating across fields' ordered character streams can capture local substring order; global pooling still limits long-range relationships and negation scope. A character encoder applied independently to words followed by unordered word pooling would not solve phrase-order loss. Compare CNN and pooling using identical retained source text, text availability, backbone, objective, sampling, seeds, checkpoint rules, and an explicitly matched total trainable-parameter budget, with actual runtime reported separately. CNN widths, filters, character vocabulary, and padding must be specified before execution; this alternative is not yet a reproducible scheduled configuration. Reordered-phrase, negation, identifier, and dimension perturbations can test representation sensitivity, not numerical understanding or recommendation accuracy. Mean-pooling invariance checks should preserve the exact token multiset and truncation boundaries.

Evaluation and uncertainty: select exclusively using the host's pinned macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, and evaluation seed 42. Report all category values and their equal-weight macro-average. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. If existing host outputs expose paired user hits, report gains/losses and bootstrap paired differences by independently resampling 200 users within each category, averaging categories equally, using 10,000 replicates and a local seed 42; report percentile 95% intervals. If user outcomes are unavailable, omit paired analysis rather than reconstructing hidden evaluator data. Intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and candidates, exclude training-seed/negative-sampling variability, and do not correct adaptive architecture or checkpoint selection. Report descriptive frequency-stratum and text-availability results only from exposed outcomes, including denominators. Fixed sampled HR does not establish full-catalog ranking quality. class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved = save_module_flags_rng_and_touched_generator_states(self.view.model)
        hooks = []
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            fixtures = isolated_training_fixtures_or_captured_immutable_batches(
                active_loader=train_loader, consume_active_loader=False,
                max_histories=8, max_candidates=100, local_seed=42)
            if fixtures is None:
                return defined_null_result('No isolated diagnostic data available')

            with torch.inference_mode(), autocast_disabled():
                results = retain_existing_probes_using_isolated_data(fixtures)
                oracle = build_unfitted_hand_specified_scoring_fixture()
                # Expected values use literal mapping tables and explicit equations.
                expected = independently_calculate_complete_scores(oracle)
                record_oracle_comparison(production_score_path(oracle), expected,
                                         atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)

                for sequence, targets, candidates in fixtures:
                    features = self.view.log2feats(sequence)
                    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
                    last = positions.expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(1)
                    valid = last.ge(0)
                    expected_readout = features[valid, last[valid]]
                    compare_production_readout_or_record_unavailable(
                        expected_readout, sequence, valid)

                    original = complete_production_logits(sequence, candidates)
                    record_relation('identity', original,
                                    complete_production_logits(sequence, candidates))
                    permutation = local_permutation(candidate_axis(candidates))
                    permuted = complete_production_logits(sequence, candidates[..., permutation])
                    record_relation('candidate_order', original,
                                    permuted[..., inverse_permutation(permutation)])
                    compare_singleton_batch_and_chunk_paths_if_contract_allows(
                        sequence, candidates, batch_sizes=[1, 3], chunk_sizes=[1, 7, 'all'])

                    for t in deterministic_valid_nonfinal_positions(sequence):
                        changed = replace_only_occupied_future_items(sequence, after=t)
                        record_relation('causal_features', features[:, :t+1],
                                        self.view.log2feats(changed)[:, :t+1])
                        record_relation('causal_complete_logits',
                            complete_logits_at_position(sequence, t, candidates),
                            complete_logits_at_position(changed, t, candidates))
                        compare_prefix_only_if_positions_and_semantics_match(sequence, t, candidates)

                for mutant in preregistered_isolated_mutants():
                    with temporary_mutation_or_record_unsupported(mutant, hooks):
                        record_exercise_evidence_and_independent_oracle_or_relation_failures(mutant)
                results.update(summarize_controls_mutations_coverage_and_cost())
                return {'metrics': results, 'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions()}
        finally:
            remove_all_hooks(hooks)
            restore_module_flags_rng_and_generator_states(saved)

                else table.detach().clone().long()
            )
            if tuple(table.shape) != (self.num_embeddings, width):

        with torch.no_grad():

            0, ids.numel(), ids.size(1), device=ids.device, dtype=torch.long

            ids.reshape(-1),

        title, description = self.title_ids[unique], self.description_ids[unique]
        present = (title.ne(0).any(-1) | description.ne(0).any(-1)) & unique.ne(0)
        rows = present.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
        with torch.autocast(device_type=identity.device.type, enabled=False):
            residual = torch.zeros_like(identity, dtype=torch.float32)
            if rows.numel():
                pooled = torch.cat(
                    [self._pool(title[rows]), self._pool(description[rows])], dim=-1
                )
                text = F.linear(pooled, self.projection.weight.float())
                direction = text / text.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(
                    self.norm_epsilon.float()
                )
                magnitude = identity[rows].float().norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).detach()
                residual = residual.index_copy(
                    0, rows, self.alpha.float().tanh() * magnitude * direction

                unique.eq(0).unsqueeze(-1), 0.0
            )
        return effective.to(identity.dtype)[inverse].reshape(
            *items.shape, self.embedding_dim
        )

    @property
    def weight(self):
        return torch.cat(
            [
                self(
                    torch.arange(
                        start,
                        min(start + 2048, self.num_embeddings),
                        device=self.id_embedding.weight.device,
                    )
                )
                for start in range(0, self.num_embeddings, 2048)

            dim=0,

class HSTUBlock(nn.Module):
    """A compact HSTU-style block: causal attention + SiLU gates + residual FFN."""

    def __init__(self, hidden_units: int, num_heads: int, dropout_rate: float):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            hidden_units,
            num_heads,
            dropout=dropout_rate,
            batch_first=True,
        )
        self.gate = nn.Linear(hidden_units, hidden_units * 2)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.ffn_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_units, hidden_units * 4),
            nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout_rate),
            nn.Linear(hidden_units * 4, hidden_units),
            nn.Dropout(dropout_rate),
        )

    def forward(
        self,
        seq_emb: torch.Tensor,
        causal_mask: torch.Tensor,
        padding_mask: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        normed = self.norm(seq_emb)
        ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Finite causal attention for left-padded histories
        batch_size, length = padding_mask.shape
        blocked = causal_mask.bool().unsqueeze(0) | padding_mask.unsqueeze(1)
        diagonal = torch.eye(length, dtype=torch.bool, device=seq_emb.device).unsqueeze(
            0
        )
        # A padded query may attend only to its own position, preventing an
        # entirely masked softmax. Valid queries still cannot attend to padding.
        blocked = blocked & ~(padding_mask.unsqueeze(2) & diagonal)
        blocked = blocked.repeat_interleave(self.attn.num_heads, dim=0)
        attn_out, _ = self.attn(
            normed,
            normed,
            normed,
            attn_mask=blocked,
            need_weights=False,
        )
        attn_out = attn_out.masked_fill(padding_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
        value, gate = self.gate(attn_out).chunk(2, dim=-1)
        seq_emb = seq_emb + self.dropout(value * F.silu(gate))
        ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Remask padded HSTU outputs
        seq_emb = seq_emb + self.ffn(self.ffn_norm(seq_emb))
        return seq_emb.masked_fill(padding_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END


class HSTURec(nn.Module):
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Configure one jointly trained lexical HSTU
    def __init__(
        self,
        itemnum: int,
        hidden_units: int = 64,
        num_blocks: int = 2,
        num_heads: int = 2,
        dropout_rate: float = 0.3,
        maxlen: int = 128,
        lexical_vocab_size: int = 2,
        title_ids=None,
        description_ids=None,
    ):
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
        super().__init__()
        if hidden_units % num_heads != 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"hidden_units={hidden_units} must be divisible by num_heads={num_heads}"
            )
        self.hidden_units = hidden_units
        self.itemnum = itemnum
        self.maxlen = maxlen
        self.item_emb = nn.Embedding(itemnum + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos_emb = nn.Embedding(maxlen + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        self.emb_dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [
                HSTUBlock(hidden_units, num_heads, dropout_rate)
                for _ in range(num_blocks)
            ]
        )
        self.last_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        with torch.no_grad():
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.item_emb.weight)
            self.item_emb.weight[0].zero_()
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.pos_emb.weight)
            self.pos_emb.weight[0].zero_()

        ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Isolated zero-gate lexical initialization and canonical effective lookup
        # The corrected backbone is fully initialized before adding text.
        # Added CPU initialization consumes no subsequent training RNG draws.
        original_identity = self.item_emb
        identity_reference = original_identity.weight.detach().clone()
        rng_reference = torch.get_rng_state().clone()
        with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
            torch.random.default_generator.manual_seed(42)
            lexical = JointLexicalEmbedding(
                original_identity, lexical_vocab_size, title_ids, description_ids
            )
        if not torch.equal(rng_reference, torch.get_rng_state()):
            raise RuntimeError("Lexical construction changed baseline RNG state")
        if not torch.equal(identity_reference, original_identity.weight.detach()):
            raise RuntimeError("Lexical construction modified identity initialization")
        self.item_emb = lexical

    def item_representation(self, items):
        return self.item_emb(items)

    def predict_score(self, features, items):
        items = torch.as_tensor(items, dtype=torch.long, device=features.device)
        candidates = self.item_emb(items)
        if items.ndim == 1:
            return torch.matmul(features, candidates.transpose(-1, -2))
        if candidates.ndim == features.ndim + 1:
            features = features.unsqueeze(-2)
        return (features * candidates).sum(dim=-1)

    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        sequence = torch.as_tensor(
            sequence, dtype=torch.long, device=self.pos_emb.weight.device
        )
        return self.forward(sequence)

    @staticmethod
    def final_features(features, sequence):
        indices = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device).unsqueeze(0)
        final = indices.masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
        selected = features[
            torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device), final.clamp_min(0)
        ]

    def forward(self, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch_size, maxlen = seq.shape
        seq_emb = self.item_emb(seq) * math.sqrt(self.hidden_units)
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
        pos = (
            torch.arange(maxlen, device=seq.device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch_size, -1)
            + 1
        )
        pos = pos * (seq != 0).long()
        seq_emb = self.emb_dropout(seq_emb + self.pos_emb(pos))
        causal_mask = torch.triu(
            torch.full((maxlen, maxlen), float("-inf"), device=seq.device), diagonal=1
        )
        padding_mask = seq == 0
        for block in self.blocks:
            seq_emb = block(seq_emb, causal_mask, padding_mask)
        ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Keep padding features exactly zero
        return self.last_norm(seq_emb).masked_fill(padding_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)
        ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END

def evaluate_val(
    model: HSTURec,
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    user_valid: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    device: torch.device,
    maxlen: int = 128,
    num_users: int = 200,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Keep validation sampling deterministic without resetting training randomness
    validation_rng = random.Random(42)
    val_users = [user for user in user_valid if user in user_train]
    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        val_users = validation_rng.sample(val_users, num_users)
    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
    if not val_users:
        return {"HR@10": 0.0, "HR@20": 0.0, "NDCG@10": 0.0, "NDCG@20": 0.0}

    hr10 = hr20 = ndcg10 = ndcg20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for user in val_users:
            pos_items = user_valid[user]
            if not pos_items:
                continue
            target = pos_items[0]
            hist = user_train[user][-maxlen:]
            seq_arr = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
            for idx, item in enumerate(reversed(hist)):
                seq_arr[maxlen - 1 - idx] = item
            interacted = set(user_train[user]) | set(pos_items)
            neg_pool = [
                item for item in range(1, itemnum + 1) if item not in interacted
            ]
            ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Use 99 unique validation negatives with an isolated RNG
            if len(neg_pool) < 99:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"User {user} has only {len(neg_pool)} eligible validation negatives; expected 99"
                )
            neg_pool = validation_rng.sample(neg_pool, 99)
            ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
            candidates = [target] + neg_pool
            seq_t = torch.tensor(seq_arr, dtype=torch.long, device=device).unsqueeze(0)
            cand_t = torch.tensor(candidates, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Validate with the canonical lexical scorer
            out = model.log2feats(seq_t)
            user_emb = model.final_features(out, seq_t)[0]
            scores = model.predict_score(user_emb, cand_t)
            ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
            rank = int(torch.argsort(scores, descending=True).tolist().index(0))
            if rank < 10:
                hr10 += 1
                ndcg10 += 1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)
            if rank < 20:
                hr20 += 1
                ndcg20 += 1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)
    denom = len(val_users)
    return {
        "HR@10": hr10 / denom,
        "HR@20": hr20 / denom,
        "NDCG@10": ndcg10 / denom,
        "NDCG@20": ndcg20 / denom,
    }

            checks[name] = value
            return value["passed"]

        def features(seq):
            executions["feature_calls"] += 1
            return self.network.log2feats(seq)

        def score(feat, ids):
            executions["score_calls"] += 1
            value = self.network.predict_score(feat, ids)
            executions["scalar_scores"] += value.numel()
            return value

        def mutation(name, actual=None, expected=None, reason=None):
            if reason is not None:
                mutants[name] = {"status": "unsupported", "reason": reason}
                return
            exercised = actual.shape != expected.shape or not torch.allclose(
                actual, expected, atol=atol, rtol=rtol
            )
            if not exercised:
                mutants[name] = {
                    "status": "unexercised",
                    "reason": "No measurable exposure under fixed tolerance",
                }
                return
            probe = "mutant/" + name
            killed = not compare(probe, actual, expected)
            mutants[name] = {
                "status": "killed" if killed else "survived",
                "observable": "complete raw scores or readout features",
                "detection_matrix": {probe: killed},
            }

        # A hand-specified unfitted fixture invokes the production score method.
        # Expected values below use literal external-ID mappings and equations.
        identity = torch.nn.Embedding(4, 2, padding_idx=0).to(self.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            identity.weight.copy_(
                torch.tensor(
                    [[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 2.0], [-2.0, 1.0], [3.0, -1.0]],
                    device=self.device,
                )
            )
        fixture_embedding = identity
        residual_coverage = {
            "covered": False,
            "reason": "Lexical fixture interface unavailable",
        }
        if type(self.network.item_emb).__name__ == "JointLexicalEmbedding" and hasattr(
            self.network.item_emb, "alpha"
        ):
            title = torch.zeros(4, 16, dtype=torch.long)
            description = torch.zeros(4, 64, dtype=torch.long)
            title[1, 0] = 2
            title[2, 0] = 3
            fixture_embedding = type(self.network.item_emb)(
                identity, 4, title, description
            ).to(self.device)
            with torch.no_grad():
                fixture_embedding.tokens.weight.zero_()
                fixture_embedding.tokens.weight[2, 0] = 1.0
                fixture_embedding.tokens.weight[3, 1] = 1.0
                fixture_embedding.projection.weight.zero_()
                fixture_embedding.projection.weight[0, 0] = 1.0
                fixture_embedding.projection.weight[1, 1] = 1.0
                fixture_embedding.alpha.fill_(float(np.arctanh(0.5)))
            residual_coverage = {
                "covered": True,
                "equation": "ID + 0.5 * norm(ID) * unit_text_direction",
            }
        literal_rows = [[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 2.0], [-2.0, 1.0], [3.0, -1.0]]
        if residual_coverage["covered"]:
            literal_rows[1][0] += 0.5 * np.sqrt(5.0)
            literal_rows[2][1] += 0.5 * np.sqrt(5.0)
        external_to_row = {701: 2, 903: 1, 211: 3}
        external_order = [701, 903, 211]
        ids = torch.tensor(
            [external_to_row[x] for x in external_order], device=self.device
        )
        known = torch.tensor([[2.0, -1.0], [-1.0, 3.0]], device=self.device)
        expected = torch.tensor(
            [
                [
                    sum(
                        float(f[d]) * literal_rows[external_to_row[x]][d]
                        for d in range(2)
                    )
                    for x in external_order
                ]
                for f in known.tolist()
            ],
            device=self.device,
        )
        production = type(self.network).predict_score
        fixture = SimpleNamespace(item_emb=fixture_embedding)
        compare("oracle/candidate_matrix", production(fixture, known, ids), expected)
        aligned_ids = torch.tensor([[2, 1], [3, 2]], device=self.device)
        aligned_feats = known[:, None, :].expand(-1, 2, -1)
        aligned_expected = torch.tensor(
            [
                [
                    sum(
                        float(known[b, d]) * literal_rows[int(aligned_ids[b, j])][d]
                        for d in range(2)
                    )
                    for j in range(2)
                ]
                for b in range(2)
            ],
            device=self.device,
        )
        compare(
            "oracle/aligned_training_scores",
            production(fixture, aligned_feats, aligned_ids),
            aligned_expected,
        )
        compare(
            "oracle/padding_zero",
            fixture_embedding(torch.tensor([0], device=self.device)),
            torch.zeros(1, 2, device=self.device),
        )
        mutation("off_by_one_ids", production(fixture, known, (ids % 3) + 1), expected)
        swapped = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3], device=self.device)
        mutation(
            "swapped_embedding_rows", production(fixture, known, swapped), expected
        )
        mutation(
            "padding_id_aliasing",
            production(fixture, known, torch.tensor([2, 0, 3], device=self.device)),
            expected,
        )

        seq = batches[0][1].to(self.device)
        # Include a short, heavily padded history and the explicit empty case.
        short = torch.zeros_like(seq[:1])
        short[0, -1] = seq[0, -1]
        seq = torch.cat([seq, short, torch.zeros_like(short)])
        feat = features(seq)
        positions = torch.arange(seq.size(1), device=self.device).expand_as(seq)
        last = positions.masked_fill(seq.eq(0), -1).amax(1)
        expected_readout = feat[
            torch.arange(len(seq), device=self.device), last.clamp_min(0)
        ]
        expected_readout = expected_readout.masked_fill(last.lt(0)[:, None], 0.0)
        readout = getattr(self.network, "final_features", None)
        if not callable(readout):
            checks["production_readout"] = {
                "passed": None,
                "reason": "No production final_features callable",
            }
            return {
                "checks": checks,
                "mutants": mutants,
                "residual_oracle": residual_coverage,
            }
        actual_readout = readout(feat, seq)
        compare("production_readout", actual_readout, expected_readout)
        candidates = [int(x) for x in batches[0][2][:, -1].tolist()]
        candidates = list(dict.fromkeys(candidates))
        rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
        remaining = np.setdiff1d(
            np.arange(1, int(self.network.itemnum) + 1), candidates
        )
        candidates += rng.choice(
            remaining, min(100 - len(candidates), len(remaining)), replace=False
        ).tolist()
        candidate_ids = torch.tensor(candidates, device=self.device, dtype=torch.long)
        original = score(actual_readout, candidate_ids)
        compare(
            "identity_complete_logits",
            score(readout(features(seq), seq), candidate_ids),
            original,
        )
        perm = torch.tensor(rng.permutation(len(candidates)), device=self.device)
        permuted = score(actual_readout, candidate_ids[perm])
        compare("candidate_order", permuted[:, torch.argsort(perm)], original)
        mutation("candidate_sort_without_inverse", permuted, original)
        for batch_size in (1, 3):
            pieces = []
            for start in range(0, len(seq), batch_size):
                part = seq[start : start + batch_size]
                pieces.append(score(readout(features(part), part), candidate_ids))
            compare(f"batch_size_{batch_size}", torch.cat(pieces), original)
        for width in (1, 7, len(candidates)):
            chunks = [
                score(actual_readout, candidate_ids[j : j + width])
                for j in range(0, len(candidates), width)
            ]
            compare(f"candidate_chunk_{width}", torch.cat(chunks, -1), original)
        mutation("batch_row_broadcast", original[:1].expand_as(original), original)
        if len(candidates) % 7:
            mutation(
                "final_chunk_omission",
                original[:, : len(candidates) // 7 * 7],
                original,
            )
        else:
            mutants["final_chunk_omission"] = {
                "status": "unexercised",
                "reason": "No partial chunk",
            }
        wrong_index = seq.ne(0).sum(1).sub(1).clamp_min(0)
        wrong = feat[torch.arange(len(seq), device=self.device), wrong_index]
        exposed = last.ge(0) & wrong_index.ne(last)
        if exposed.any():
            mutation(
                "count_minus_one_readout", wrong[exposed], expected_readout[exposed]
            )
        else:
            mutants["count_minus_one_readout"] = {
                "status": "unexercised",
                "reason": "Indices coincide",
            }
        causal_positions = []
        for row in range(len(seq)):
            occupied = seq[row].ne(0).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
            if len(occupied) < 2 or int(self.network.itemnum) < 2:
                continue
            t = int(occupied[0])
            changed = seq[row : row + 1].clone()
            future = occupied[occupied > t]
            changed[0, future] = changed[0, future] % int(self.network.itemnum) + 1
            altered = features(changed)
            compare(
                f"causal_features/{row}",
                altered[:, : t + 1],
                feat[row : row + 1, : t + 1],
            )
            compare(
                f"causal_complete_logits/{row}",
                score(altered[:, t], candidate_ids),
                score(feat[row : row + 1, t], candidate_ids),
            )
            causal_positions.append(
                {"row": row, "position": t, "future_slots": future.tolist()}
            )
        mutation(
            "disabled_causal_mask",
            reason="No isolated supported causal-mask mutation hook; trained network is not patched",
        )
        mutation(
            "wrong_category_routing",
            reason="Category routing belongs to generated predictor, not ModelView",
        )
        exercised = [
            m for m in mutants.values() if m["status"] in ("killed", "survived")
        ]
        return {
            "protocol_version": "hstu-contracts-v1",
            "atol": atol,
            "rtol": rtol,
            "checks": checks,
            "mutants": mutants,
            "mutation_summary": {
                "killed": sum(m["status"] == "killed" for m in exercised),
                "exercised_non_equivalent": len(exercised),
                "scope": "Listed diagnostic outputs only; no checkpoints mutated",
            },
            "residual_oracle": residual_coverage,
            "fixtures": {
                "sequences": seq.cpu().tolist(),
                "ordered_candidates": candidates,
                "causal_positions": causal_positions,
                "complete_reference_logits": original.cpu().tolist(),
            },
            "executions": executions,
            "prefix_only": {
                "passed": None,
                "reason": "Compacting prefixes shifts learned absolute positions",
            },
            "deployment_parity": {
                "passed": None,
                "reason": "ModelView exposes no pre-save capture or fresh-process generated-predictor integration; no deployment parity claimed",
            },
            "mapping_parity": {
                "passed": None,
                "reason": "Synthetic external mapping is tested; real public mapping and checkpoint/category metadata are not exposed",
            },
            "tie_rule": "Auxiliary diagnostics use descending score then ascending item ID; host tie rule unavailable",
            "empty_history_policy": "Production final_features is compared to explicit zero readout",
            "scoring_contract": "1D items -> shared candidate axis; B x L items with B x L x D features -> aligned scores",
        }
